public_rationale: Research during GPT-4's first year documented hallucinations, elementary mistakes, and substantial changes in behavior. A February 2024 provider incident also documented incoherent output. These support the modest claim that such problems continued to occur. The February bug was fixed, and none of these records establishes that improvements were absent or that the problems are permanently insoluble.
limitations: The research tests selected tasks rather than representative everyday usage.
The incident record identifies ChatGPT and an infrastructure fault, without naming the affected model version.
‘Have lingered’ is assessed as recurring failure modes over the retrospective year, not as a claim that every cited defect remained active on the post date.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Hallucinations, instability and occasional nonsensical errors remain unsolved in GPT-4 class LLMs.

statement.excerpt: Some core problems have lingered, particularly hallucinations, instability and occasional nonsensical errors.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that these failure modes continued to occur, not that performance never improved or that every model failed equally often.
Hallucinations are unsupported or false assertions. Instability includes material changes in answers or behavior across prompts, service updates, or deployments.
Nonsensical errors include plainly incoherent output and elementary mistakes inconsistent with a model's otherwise demonstrated abilities.
The birthday retrospective supplies the preceding year as the reporting period. Evidence must concern models or services operating during that year.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations and operational records document continuing hallucinations, materially variable behavior, and occasional incoherent or elementary errors in GPT-4-class systems during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes that the named failure modes had been eliminated by publication. Lower error rates or a repair to one incident alone would not contradict persistence.

evidence.explanation: The experiments demonstrate false supporting assertions that GPT-4 can recognize as wrong when asked separately. They establish hallucination and elementary-error failure modes, not a population-wide error rate.
Comparisons of March and June service versions found material changes across tasks. Some results improved, so this supports instability rather than uniform deterioration.

evidence.locator: Incident write-up, explanation of the February 20 failure
evidence.explanation: OpenAI explains that a deployment bug produced word sequences that made no sense. This documents a contemporary service failure, not proof that the underlying model architecture necessarily produces nonsense.
The specific deployment incident was repaired before Marcus's post. It cannot establish that this particular bug remained active on March 16.
